claims.text: The untreated refractory high-entropy alloys have limited ductility.
The untreated refractory high-entropy alloys have limited uniform deformability.
Composition changes can tailor unstable fault energies in refractory high-entropy alloys.
Tailoring unstable fault energies through composition changes can produce metastable alloys exhibiting transformation-induced plasticity.
Tailoring unstable fault energies through composition changes can produce metastable alloys exhibiting twinning-induced plasticity.
Transformation-induced plasticity enhances the strength-ductility synergy of refractory high-entropy alloys.
Twinning-induced plasticity enhances the strength-ductility synergy of refractory high-entropy alloys.
Tailoring unstable fault energies through composition changes improves ductility relative to untreated refractory high-entropy alloys.
Tailoring unstable fault energies through composition changes improves uniform deformability relative to untreated refractory high-entropy alloys.
The ductility and uniform-deformability improvements occur without sacrificing high strength.
The ductility and uniform-deformability improvements occur without sacrificing impact-induced energy release.
The proposed improvements should hold under high-stress conditions.
The proposed improvements should hold under high-strain-rate conditions.
